agency.name: Toyama Chitetsu Bus (富山地方鉄道バス)
agency.operating_note: Toyama Chiho Railroad's regional route-bus network. The official catalog also publishes keyless TripUpdates and VehiclePositions.

findings.effort: A column in stops.txt; your scheduling software likely has it.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_boarding to 1 (accessible) or 2 (not accessible) for every stop. A field survey can start with the busiest stops.
findings.what: 1034 of 1034 stops don't say whether a wheelchair user can board there.
findings.why: Riders who use wheelchairs can't plan a trip when accessibility is marked 'unknown'; apps show no information at all.

findings.effort: A default or per-trip field in your export.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_accessible on every trip. If every vehicle is accessible, this may be one default; otherwise use the value for each trip.
findings.what: 1354 of 1354 trips don't say whether the vehicle is wheelchair accessible.
findings.why: Even with accessible stops, riders need to know the bus itself can take them.

completeness.name: completeness
completeness.summary: 0% of stops state wheelchair accessibility (0% marked accessible, 0% marked not accessible). This measures what the feed publishes, not whether a stop is physically usable. Fare data is published.

findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'duplicate_key' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Duplicate key (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: A planned ID change, not a quick text cleanup.
findings.fix: Only change the flagged IDs if an app needs basic ASCII values. Update each place that uses the ID. Keep all names and headsigns in their original language.
findings.what: Some internal IDs use characters outside the basic text set.
findings.why: These IDs are valid UTF-8 data. This warning is only about support in older apps. It does not mean that names in other languages are wrong.

findings.effort: Often a bulk fix in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Use mixed case for stop names and headsigns (e.g. 'Main St & 2nd Ave', not 'MAIN ST & 2ND AVE').
findings.what: Some rider-facing names are in ALL CAPS or all lowercase.
findings.why: ALL-CAPS stop and headsign names are harder to read in apps and are read awkwardly by screen readers.

findings.fix: Give each route a distinct short or long name.
findings.what: Two or more routes share the same name.
findings.why: Riders can't tell the routes apart in apps.

findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'route_short_name_too_long' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Route short name too long (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

correctness.name: correctness
correctness.summary: The MobilityData validator flagged 5 kinds of issue across 97564 instances (2 error, 97562 warning, 0 informational).

freshness.name: freshness
freshness.summary: Service data covers the next 292 days.

findings.fix: Ask your AVL vendor to publish updates at least every 20 seconds (the Caltrans guideline).
findings.what: Realtime data was up to 2974 seconds old when sampled.
findings.why: Stale positions and predictions are worse than none: riders watch a bus that already left.

realtime.name: realtime
realtime.summary: Sampled 6 times outside service hours: 2 of 2 configured feeds healthy; vehicle position plausibility was not measurable.

notes: All four score categories were measured this run.
Realtime was sampled in one bounded window of 6 snapshots.
The feed was downloaded from the agency's own URL.

criteria.detail: Service data covers the next 293 days.
States wheelchair access on 0% of stops and 0% of trips; the mark needs 90% of each.

conformance.summary: This feed is close to the conformance mark. 1 validator error to resolve. States wheelchair access on 0% of stops and 0% of trips; the mark needs 90% of each.

scoring_profile.provenance: GTFS Scorecard's project-authored weights, deductions, thresholds, grade bands, and fix ranking, informed by the California Transit Data Guidelines and the MobilityData gtfs-validator. It is not a worldwide standard or a compliance determination.

top_fixes.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'duplicate_key' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
top_fixes.what: Duplicate key (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
top_fixes.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

top_fixes.fix: Ask your AVL vendor to publish updates at least every 20 seconds (the Caltrans guideline).
top_fixes.what: Realtime data was up to 2974 seconds old when sampled.
top_fixes.why: Stale positions and predictions are worse than none: riders watch a bus that already left.

top_fixes.effort: A column in stops.txt; your scheduling software likely has it.
top_fixes.fix: Set wheelchair_boarding to 1 (accessible) or 2 (not accessible) for every stop. A field survey can start with the busiest stops.
top_fixes.what: 1034 of 1034 stops don't say whether a wheelchair user can board there.
top_fixes.why: Riders who use wheelchairs can't plan a trip when accessibility is marked 'unknown'; apps show no information at all.
